canonical_definition: Language Modeling is the ability of a computational system to model and predict next-token distributions in text sequences, typically operationalized through autoregressive language modeling where the model learns to predict subsequent tokens based on preceding context. This capability is most commonly evaluated using perplexity metrics across diverse text corpora, reflecting the model's capacity to capture statistical patterns and generate grammatically structured continuations, though some definitions emphasize its role in downstream task generalization or text completion rather than purely next-token prediction.
